name: parametric-cad-design
title: Designing in Fusion
description: Use when designing or modelling in Fusion through the fusion-essentials tools - building a part, a surfaced product, an assembly, or a machining job, not running a fixed procedure. Practice read out of Autodesk's own sample designs: what to settle before the first feature, how a sketch carries intent, the feature order of a moulded or surfaced part, how an assembly's freedom is structured, and which machining strategy fits. Rules say when they apply and what to read back; recipes are ordered tool sequences with a bar for done and an exemplar to X-ray.
summary: Rules for judgment, recipes for sequence, a bar for done - read out of the designs Autodesk ships as samples.

sections.title: Kernel - every design
sections.use_when: always - the five habits that hold on every brief

rules.do: write what the design must satisfy and each interface as a checkable number - seating faces, aligned axes, clearance, wall thickness
rules.except: a throwaway probe

prove.observe: the active document, its units and what is already in it

rules.do: decide the feature order before drawing: form, then fillets, then shell, then bosses and holes, then cosmetics - a timeline built in that order edits cleanly, one built by accretion does not
rules.except: a one-feature part

prove.observe: the timeline reads as the order you planned

rules.do: type a wall thickness or a pitch ONCE and reference it by name everywhere else; promote it to a named parameter only when a family or a configuration is expected
rules.except: a measured value, held in one parameter saying so

prove.observe: dimensions whose expression is another dimension's name, not a repeated literal

rules.do: read it back against intent before the next feature: a bounding box, a volume, a screenshot - never only at the end
rules.except: a milestone a write already verified

prove.observe: bounding box and volume against the numbers you wrote down

rules.do: compare it with the acceptance you wrote and say what you could not meet; a screenshot that reads as the object is part of the acceptance
rules.except: acceptance the brief left open

prove.observe: does it read as the object it should be

sections.title: Plan
sections.use_when: before the first component exists - naming, variants, what is bought

rules.do: a made part takes a functional name, a bought part its spec - 'SS 6003 2RS (10 X 17 X 35mm)', 'SHCS M8 X 65mm' - so the browser is the bill of materials
rules.except: imported names

prove.observe: no 'Component1' and no 'Sketch1' left in the tree

rules.do: author them as configurations of one document driven by a few named parameters and a part-number property; check the active row before calling a failed compute a defect
rules.except: a single variant

prove.observe: the configuration table, its columns and the active row

rules.example: the Configured Dumbbell: 14 rows varying weight_width, weight_length, weight_text and a Part Number

rules.when: a purchased, imported or generative body enters the design
rules.do: hold it as a base feature in its own component and re-cut only the interfaces on top of it with hole and chamfer features; never edit the frozen body
rules.except: a body you are modelling yourself

prove.observe: the timeline: a BaseFeature row, then Hole rows on the same component

sections.title: Sketch
sections.use_when: any profile that must survive a size change or drive a feature

rules.when: a profile has symmetry, equal spacing or a family of equal features
rules.do: draw the construction line, then constrain: symmetry about it, midpoint on it, equal between the members; dimensions pin only what remains
rules.except: a one-off reference sketch

prove.observe: more constraints than dimensions, and is_fully_constrained true

rules.example: a knife layout: 43 constraints, 5 dimensions; a handle profile: ten symmetry constraints, six expressions

rules.do: put the origin on a midpoint or at the crossing of two construction diagonals, never at a typed coordinate
rules.except: geometry projected from a body, which is already placed

prove.observe: a midpoint or coincident constraint naming the origin point

rules.do: type it once and write the other dimensions as that dimension's name (d239) or a named parameter
rules.except: two sizes that only happen to match today

prove.observe: dimension expressions referencing a name, not a repeated number

rules.when: an outline is a free curve
rules.do: draw a control-point spline and make its ends smooth to construction lines whose angles and lengths are dimensioned; the control polygon, not the curve, carries the intent
rules.except: a one-off path nothing else references, where a fit-point spline is enough

prove.observe: a cv_spline with 'smooth' constraints to lines that carry angle dimensions

rules.when: a clip, rib or pocket must follow an existing wall
rules.do: project the wall's edges into the sketch and dimension the detail by offset from them; projected geometry has no freedom, so few constraints fully constrain the sketch
rules.except: detail on a plane no body touches

prove.observe: fixed_spline or projected entities plus offset dimensions, is_fully_constrained true

rules.when: a derived length or angle matters to the brief
rules.do: add it as a driven dimension and read it back; a master sketch may stay not fully constrained only where its free entities are the splines
rules.except: a sketch nobody will edit

prove.observe: dimensions with driving=false carrying the value the brief asked for

recipes.title: An anchored, symmetric profile
recipes.use_when: a bracket, plate or revolved profile that must resize by intent

steps.do: create the sketch on the origin plane the part is symmetric about
draw one construction line through the origin as the symmetry axis
draw the outline as lines and arcs on ONE side, plus the circles for bores
midpoint of the base line on the origin; symmetry of each mirrored pair about the axis; tangent between arcs and their lines; equal between features meant to match
one dimension per independent size; write repeated sizes as another dimension's name
X-ray the sketch
steps.read_back: is_fully_constrained true; constraints outnumber dimensions; the profile areas you expect

bar.measure: sketch_get reports is_fully_constrained true and changing one dimension moves both symmetric halves
bar.eyes: the profile reads as the part's silhouette with the origin on its symmetry line

exemplar.look_at: Handle/Sketch1 - 17 lines held by 10 symmetry constraints and 6 expressions such as length_handle / 2 + length_thread
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

recipes.title: A link profile between bores
recipes.use_when: a rocker, lever, connecting link or any web joining round bosses

steps.do: one circle per bore at each pivot, and a concentric outer circle per boss
concentric each bore with its boss; coincident the bore centres with construction points or projected pivot geometry
two lines per web, roughly tangent between neighbouring bosses, and one large arc closing the outer edge
tangent each web line to both bosses it joins; tangent the closing arc to its lines
bore and boss diameters, the closing arc radius, and the pivot spacing
X-ray
steps.read_back: fully constrained; the web profiles are closed regions between bosses

bar.measure: sketch_get: is_fully_constrained true and one closed profile per web plus one per boss annulus
bar.eyes: the outline is the classic link: round ends joined by tangent flanks

exemplar.look_at: ROCKER/Sketch1 - three bores, eight tangent constraints, one R70 closing arc, four dimensions
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

recipes.title: An organic outline that edits by intent
recipes.use_when: a mouse, handle or shell silhouette that must stay smooth while its proportions change

steps.do: draw a cv_spline (degree 5) through the silhouette's control points - it lays its control polygon down as construction lines
steps.read_back: the built degree (a degree the API cannot honour is clamped) and the polygon line ids

steps.do: one construction guide line at each end, in the tangent direction
at each end: coincident the guide line's end with the spline's end FIRST, then smooth between them - a smooth moves the end point, so smooth without coincident fails at the second end
angle each guide line and dimension the polygon's spacing
the overall length as a DRIVEN dimension
X-ray
steps.read_back: degree 5 and two smooth constraints; only the spline's interior is free

bar.measure: sketch_get lists smooth constraints at both ends and the driven overall length matches the brief
bar.eyes: the curve reads as one continuous sweep with no kink where it meets a guide

exemplar.look_at: Mouse/Side Profile - a degree-5 spline G2-smooth to guides at 35, 40, 30 and 50 deg; Top Profile the same at degree 7
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

sections.title: Model
sections.use_when: turning sketches into a part - order, carving, patterns, frozen bodies

rules.when: a moulded or cast part is built
rules.do: build the outer form, fillet its edges, shell it LAST among the form features, then add bosses, ribs, drafts and holes, then cosmetic split faces
rules.except: a machined block, where holes may precede fillets

prove.observe: Shell after the fillets and before the bosses in the timeline

rules.when: the form is a block with a curved face or a tapered body
rules.do: extrude the block, loft or extrude the cutting form, split the block by it and remove the waste - the kept piece carries clean faces
rules.except: a form that is itself one extrude or revolve

prove.observe: one body left with the volume you expect after the split

rules.do: model one half against the symmetry plane, mirror it, combine into one body
rules.except: asymmetric detail added after the mirror

prove.observe: a Mirror row followed by a Combine row

rules.do: build one and pattern it; copies answering different requirements are modelled apart
rules.except: copies that merely share a shape

prove.observe: the pattern feature in the timeline with the count you asked for

rules.do: take draft, wall thickness, minimum internal radius and hole sizes from the process; a 0.05 mm face offset is a fit clearance, a chord-length fillet is a cosmetic edge
rules.except: an unsettled process, which is stated rather than assumed

prove.observe: face normals show the draft; fillet radii meet the minimum

rules.do: use the thread feature for a standard thread that a drawing or a tap will define; sweep a section along a helix with a pipe only when the ridge itself must be solid geometry
rules.except: a cosmetic thread nothing mates with

prove.observe: a Thread row, or a Sweep plus Pipe pair, not both

rules.when: bodies are still being carved out of one another
rules.do: stay in bodies until the part count settles, then promote each body to a named component before any joint
rules.except: a part known from the brief, which starts as its own component

prove.observe: no unnamed 'Component' rows; every joint follows the component rows

recipes.title: A moulded shell part in the right order
recipes.use_when: a basket, cover, drawer front or housing with a wall, bosses and clips

steps.do: extrude the footprint into a block taller than the part
loft the crowned form between two sections (a rectangle with one edge a large tangent arc)
split the block by the form and remove the waste
fillet the outer edges, largest radius first
shell to the wall thickness, opening the open face
steps.read_back: volume dropped to about wall area times thickness

steps.do: bosses and ribs from a sketch on a plane inside the wall
draft the bosses toward the pull direction
screw holes sized for the fastener
section through a boss
steps.read_back: one uniform wall, boss root filleted

bar.measure: model_inspect volume is wall area times thickness within 10 percent and view_section shows one uniform wall
bar.eyes: smooth and crowned outside; bosses and ribs on a thin wall inside

exemplar.look_at: rows 0-19: Extrude, Loft, Split, RemoveBody, Draft, Fillet x4, then Shell1; bosses, drafts and a second shell follow
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

recipes.title: A frozen body with re-cut interfaces
recipes.use_when: a purchased part, an imported STEP or a generative outcome that needs holes and seats

steps.do: make a component named by the part's spec
start a base feature in it
import the STEP or other file into that component
finish the base feature
steps.read_back: the timeline shows one BaseFeature row

steps.do: align the body to the origin and the interface axes
steps.read_back: model_inspect bounding box centred where intended

steps.do: sketch the hole pattern on the mounting face
cut the holes as hole features, counterbored where a screw head seats
chamfer the interface edges
read the timeline
steps.read_back: BaseFeature, Move, Sketch, Hole, Chamfer - nothing edits the frozen body itself

bar.measure: design_get shows the base feature followed only by interface features; model_measure_between gives the hole spacing the brief asked for
bar.eyes: the organic or bought body is untouched; the holes sit on flat pads

exemplar.look_at: seven rows: BaseFeature1, Align1, DeleteFace2, Sketch1, Hole1, Sketch2, Hole2 on a generative outcome
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

steps.do: the driving sizes as named parameters (length_handle, diameter_thread), the derived ones as ratios (chamfer_size = weight_width / 8)
write every profile dimension as a parameter expression, halves as diameter / 2
revolve the profile, or extrude with a profile offset for a coating
create the label, then bind it with parameter=<the text parameter>
emboss that bound text
steps.read_back: the text lands raised or engraved by the signed depth

steps.do: save the document - a configuration table refuses an unsaved one
create the table, a column per varying size, a row per variant; a text column takes no per-row value, so relabel by param_set
steps.read_back: configured true, then each column id

steps.do: activate a different row
read the configurations slice and the timeline
steps.read_back: the row reads active and the timeline is healthy

bar.measure: param_get shows only named parameters and ratios; design_get reports healthy on each configuration row
bar.eyes: switching rows changes size and label together with no broken feature

exemplar.look_at: 12 parameters, urethane_coating = weight_width / 10, weight_text driving the emboss, 14 configuration rows

sections.title: Surface
sections.use_when: a shell, skin or product form that no extrude or revolve describes

rules.when: the outer form is the product
rules.do: build the skin as surfaces - sweep, loft, patch - then trim, stitch once with a stated tolerance and thicken once; the solid comes last
rules.except: a form one solid feature already describes

prove.observe: Stitch and Thicken rows after every surface row, not between them

rules.do: extend the cutting surface a few millimetres past the body first, so the trim never lands on an edge
rules.except: a cutter that already overhangs

prove.observe: an Extend row immediately before the Trim row

rules.when: two skins must meet with a smooth transition
rules.do: split the faces where the blend starts, delete the faces between, and loft between the split edges; a fillet only where the transition is a constant radius
rules.except: a constant-radius corner

prove.observe: no crease: adjacent face normals agree along the seam

rules.when: several parts share one outer form
rules.do: keep the skin in a master document with named skeleton sketches; each part derives it and closes it with a boundary fill, then adds its own walls, bosses and clips
rules.except: a single-part shell

prove.observe: each part's timeline starts with a derive row then a BoundaryFill row

rules.when: the quickest form is a solid but only some faces are wanted
rules.do: delete the faces you do not want; the remaining skin is the surface to build on
rules.except: a solid you will keep whole

prove.observe: the tree's body row reads is_solid false after the delete

recipes.title: A swept and surfaced bottle
recipes.use_when: a container whose section changes along a curved spine, its neck narrower than the body

steps.do: 'Bottle_Bottom' on XY: an ellipse dimensioned by its radii
'Bottle_Profiles' on XZ: spine arc, offset rail, cv_spline neck
loft the ellipse to the neck section with the rails, as_surface true
'Bottle_Crown' on XZ: the shoulder profile, body radius to neck
revolve the profile about the bottle axis
extend the NECK until it crosses the crown
trim ONLY where the crown crosses the body, keeping that cell
stitch the two at 0.1 mm
shell to the wall, opening the mouth
chord-length fillets on the shoulder
offset the mouth face -0.05 mm

bar.measure: became_solid true, a Shell row after the stitch, one body
bar.eyes: a smooth leaning body with a crowned shoulder and no facet at the crown

exemplar.look_at: Sweep1 with a rail, Top_Crown on projected edges, Extend 5 mm before Trim, Stitch 0.10 mm, chord fillets, OffsetFaces -0.05 mm

recipes.title: One skin, several parts
recipes.use_when: a product whose top, base and middle share one outer surface

steps.do: named skeleton sketches in the master: side, top and section profiles as cv_splines smooth to dimensioned guides
steps.read_back: each sketch named; zero profiles is expected

steps.do: loft the skin between the section profiles with the side and top profiles as rails
mirror the half skin about the symmetry plane
stitch the halves
steps.read_back: one surface body; became_solid false is fine for a skin

steps.do: in each part document, derive the master's skin body
steps.read_back: the derived body and its source version

steps.do: extrude the parting line into a surface through the skin
boundary fill with the skin and the parting surface as the tools, keeping the part's cell
shell to the wall thickness
offset the mating faces for fit clearance

bar.measure: each part's design_get starts with a derive row and a BoundaryFill row, and model_inspect gives one solid
bar.eyes: the parts assemble into the skin with no step at the parting line

exemplar.look_at: the Mouse master's five named profiles; Base, Middle and Top each open with Context1 (derive) and BoundaryFill1

sections.title: Assemble
sections.use_when: more than one component - how they are held, joined and moved

rules.do: pick one idiom for the document - joints, or assembly constraints plus rigid groups - and keep it; mixing them is why large timelines read as noise
rules.except: a rigid group over an already-joined sub-mechanism

prove.observe: joint_count and relations agree with the idiom you chose

rules.when: an assembly has a fixed moving mechanism
rules.do: establish one intentional reference path from the grounded part; do not ground parts to hide missing joints
rules.except: floating or multiple independent mechanisms

prove.observe: one ground_to_parent root and every joint reachable from it

rules.when: a part was modelled against its neighbours where it sits
rules.do: join it with as-built joints - nothing moves - and let the joint limits carry the stroke
rules.except: a part placed from elsewhere, which takes a joint with joint origins

prove.observe: the joint's limits hold the travel the brief named

rules.when: a joint needs a flip or an offset
rules.do: use the joint's align angle and align offset; do not add spacer bodies to fix a pose
rules.except: a real spacer part in the bill of materials

prove.observe: the joint's frame sits where the offset put it, and the occurrence list holds no spacer that is not a real part

rules.when: the mechanism has a driven joint
rules.do: drive it to home and a representative extreme; keep moving joints few, the rest rigid; link two joints with a motion link when one motion implies the other
rules.except: a joint with no travel of interest

prove.observe: the value at each pose
overlaps at each pose, intended fit or defect

rules.example: a nut overlapping a plain shaft is a thread modelled as a cylinder

rules.do: expect a set of adsk_ parameters per fastener and read only the authored set; name each fastener instance by its spec
rules.except: a design with no library parts

prove.observe: the authored user parameters are what comes back and generated_skipped counts the adsk_ ones the fasteners minted; include_generated=true lists those

recipes.title: A part modelled in place and joined as built
recipes.use_when: a rocker, bracket or lever designed between parts that already sit where they belong

steps.do: a new component named for the part, activated
project the neighbours' bores and faces into the new sketch
the link profile between the projected bores (see the link recipe)
extrude the profile to the part thickness
steps.read_back: one body in the new component

steps.do: counterbored holes for the screws
a revolute as-built joint to each bearing it pivots on; a cylindrical one where it also slides
steps.read_back: the joint reports its motion type

steps.do: set the limits to the stroke the brief names
drive to each extreme
check at each pose

bar.measure: assembly_get lists the as-built joints with the limits set, and joint_drive reaches both extremes without interference
bar.eyes: the link sits on its bearings and swings through its arc

exemplar.look_at: rows 111-124: ROCKER sketched between bearings, three as-built joints, extrude, fillet, mirror, holes, a fourth as-built joint
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

recipes.title: A screw cap that turns and travels
recipes.use_when: a threaded cap, lead screw or any turn-to-advance pair

steps.do: ground the body part to its parent
a revolute joint between the turning part and the body on the thread axis
a slider joint between the advancing part and the body along the same axis - a second joint on the SAME pair is refused as over-constrained
slide limits equal to the travel
link the revolute to the slider with ratio = pitch / 360 (mm of slide per degree)
drive the revolute 90 deg - a full 360 is an equivalent pose and moves nothing

bar.measure: after a 90 deg drive assembly_get's value_now reads 90 on the revolute and a quarter pitch on the slider
bar.eyes: the advancing part moves along the axis as the other turns

exemplar.look_at: Motion Link 5 over two cylindrical joints on one pair - made in the UI; through the API one pair takes one joint

sections.title: Validate
sections.use_when: the geometry exists and must be proved against the brief

rules.do: measure each and report the number - contact where parts engage, clearance where they move
rules.except: an interface the brief left open

prove.observe: the distance or angle at each interface

rules.do: read plane normals, axis directions and containment, then look: a flat stack passes every count while nothing nests, and a brick passes every measurement while looking nothing like the product
rules.except: a genuinely planar design

prove.observe: face normals and linear-edge directions
the silhouette reads as the object

rules.when: a measurement disagrees with the brief
rules.do: report the disagreement - a measurement is evidence about the artifact; intent comes from the brief
rules.except: a brief quoting a measured fact about existing hardware

prove.observe: the measured value beside the brief's

rules.do: confirm the effect through a read other than the tool's claim; read a refusal's reason before retrying
rules.except: a deferred write, confirmed through the poller it names

prove.observe: the timeline entry the write claims

rules.do: leave the saved state valid, name the sketches and components, look at the result, and say what you could not do
rules.except: a scratch document

prove.observe: the document's save state

sections.title: Manufacture
sections.use_when: a machining job - setups, strategy choice, what a toolpath must prove

rules.do: hold the fixture as its own components beside the part, select only the part body as the model, and take the work coordinate system from the stock; the fixture is geometry the toolpaths must avoid, not decoration
rules.except: a setup sheet exercise with no fixture

prove.observe: selected_models names the part only and the wcs origin_mode is stated

rules.do: parallel finishes shallow areas and skips steep ones by default; 3D contour does the opposite; one flag on each takes the other's areas, and scallop finishes both at a constant stepover a tenth of the tool
rules.except: a flat part, where face and 2D contour suffice

prove.observe: machineSteepAreas or machineShallowAreas is the only difference between the pair

rules.do: adaptive takes deep stepdowns at a light radial load and needs no leads or compensation; 2D pocket takes shallow stepdowns with a finishing pass and cutter compensation - pick adaptive for bulk removal, pocket when the wall finish comes from the same operation
rules.except: a slot, which wants the slot strategy on a closed slot contour

prove.observe: optimalLoad and maximumStepdown on adaptive; finishing passes and compensation on pocket

rules.do: compare their geometry selections - chains, extension modes, stock contours, boundaries - because a parameter diff cannot see them
rules.except: operations that differ in parameters already

prove.observe: each operation's references: the chains and faces it was given

rules.when: a turning profile finishing cycle generates carrying a warning
rules.do: 'Lead-Out has been modified due to a gouge with the remaining stock' says the exit move ran into stock the cycle leaves behind, and Fusion moved it rather than refusing. Measured on a turned flange, each remedy cleared it: doLeadOut false, or useStockToLeave true with xStockToLeave and zStockToLeave at 0.5mm. Take the allowance on a cycle a later pass follows; turn the lead-out off on the last one
rules.except: a cycle whose exit move has to clear a face, where the lead-out is the point

prove.observe: operations_with_warnings is empty for that setup and none of its operations is in empty_toolpaths

rules.when: a milling setup takes stock_mode 'previous_setup' after a turning setup
rules.do: MEASURED on a turned flange, one whole-model adaptive with its parameters untouched: it generated EMPTY on that setup under previous_setup stock in both the 'rest' and 'setupStockSilhouette' modes, and the same operation cut 347 s the moment the setup alone was switched to a relative box. These stock extents keep the relative-box numbers and describe nothing this setup cuts, so size a clearing strategy from the preceding setup's own operations, not from these extents. An operation's OWN rest is a separate knob: defineStockBy 'rest' reads restMaterialSource 'previousOperations' - the operations before it in THIS setup, not the setup's stock mode - and with every sibling valid it computes, no 'Failed to generate rest material.' among the warnings
rules.except: the first setup of a job, whose stock is the billet

prove.observe: the setup row reads stock_mode 'previous_setup' and stock_extents_describe says the box is not the stock
whether the clearing operation is named in empty_toolpaths - the list reports membership, never why

recipes.title: Choosing a strategy for a feature
recipes.use_when: a face, pocket, wall, hole or free-form surface needs an operation

steps.do: read the setup's allowed strategies
steps.read_back: allowed true for the candidates; a false one cannot be created

steps.do: classify the feature: flat top (face), pocket floor, wall (2D contour), hole (drill, bore, thread), curved surface (parallel, contour, scallop), edge (chamfer)
create the candidate with a named tool
give it the chains or faces, with the chain extension where the cut runs past the wall
generate
steps.read_back: a handle, then cam_get_status until completed

steps.do: inspect the result
steps.read_back: the operation is not among empty_toolpaths; an empty one is the wrong strategy or selection

steps.do: read the time slice
when unsure between two strategies, compare the pair: pocket and adaptive differ in 114 parameters, optimalLoad and stepdown among them
steps.read_back: the parameters that differ name the trade-off

bar.measure: cam_inspect_toolpaths lists no empty toolpath, the time slice reads above zero, and the operation is valid with no warning
bar.eyes: the toolpath covers the feature and nothing else

exemplar.look_at: 22 operations named for their variant, '2D Contour2' beside its multiple-passes, Trimmed and Rest siblings
exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

recipes.title: Proving a toolpath before posting
recipes.use_when: an operation generated and must be trusted

steps.do: read the operation with its parameters and tool
steps.read_back: state valid, no warning text, the tool it uses

steps.do: read the toolpath census
steps.read_back: the operation is valid and not empty

steps.do: read the time slice
steps.read_back: machining time above zero, feed and rapid distances

steps.do: show the toolpath and take a screenshot
steps.read_back: the passes lie on the feature, inside the stock

steps.do: post to a scratch folder with the machine's post
steps.read_back: the file landed with a size above zero

steps.do: re-read after posting
steps.read_back: no operation went out of date

bar.measure: the time slice reads above zero, the census lists the operation as not empty, and the posted file exists with a size
bar.eyes: the shown toolpath stays on the feature, inside the stock and clear of the fixture

recipes.title: Drilling across the turned axis
recipes.use_when: a hole whose axis runs across the part axis - a cross-drilling, or a hole through a boss on a turned part

steps.do: find the hole's own cylindrical face
steps.read_back: its 'axis', which is not the milling setup's Z

steps.do: give that axis a setup of its own: one per hole axis, so opposed holes are two setups, never one bore through both
steps.read_back: the setup name and zero operations

steps.do: bind the setup's Z to that face: wcs={'z_axis': <the handle>}
create the drilling cycle
aim it with selection='holes' and the same face
generate, then read the status
steps.read_back: on world Z it errors 'Cylindrical face not in tool orientation!'; bound to the face it errors 'Selected face may not be safe for cutting at current tool orientation!' - the bound axis points into the material

steps.do: turn the axis round: parameters={'wcs_orientation_flipZ': 'true'}
regenerate
read the time slice
steps.read_back: machining time above zero for the drill

bar.measure: the operation carries no error and its machining time reads above zero
bar.eyes: the drill enters square to its face and stops in the material, not through to the far side
